options.metric: Annual count of recorded motorist deaths
options.reason: Annual fatality counts directly show the recorded fatality burden over time.
options.answer: The file cannot show per-mile risk, but recorded motorist deaths declined 26% from 110 in 2013 to 81 in 2025.
options.interpretation: This shows the annual fatality-count component of the question: recorded motorist deaths were lower in 2025 than in 2013, though the series rose sharply in 2020. Counts are a direct fatality-burden measure, but they leave per-mile risk and changes in driving exposure unanswered.

options.metric: Recorded motorist deaths per 1,000 crash records
options.denominator: All police-reported crash records in that year
options.reason: Normalizing deaths by crash records shows whether recorded fatalities changed relative to the number of recorded crashes.
options.answer: The file cannot show per-mile risk; motorist deaths per 1,000 crash records rose from 0.54 in 2013 to 0.95 in 2025 (75%).
options.interpretation: This reframes risk as recorded fatalities relative to reported crashes, and the rate is higher in 2025 than in 2013. It is defensible as a fatality burden per crash record, but crash records are not miles driven, so it does not establish per-mile risk.

options.metric: Crash records with at least one motorist death per 100,000 crash records
options.denominator: All police-reported crash records in that year
options.reason: Counting fatal crashes rather than individual deaths measures the frequency of a crash involving a motorist death.
options.answer: The file cannot show per-mile risk; crashes with a motorist death rose from 50.1 to 87.7 per 100,000 crash records between 2013 and 2025 (75%).
options.interpretation: This shows how often a recorded crash involved at least one motorist death; that recorded-crash rate is higher in 2025 than in 2013. It is defensible as fatal-crash incidence among reported crashes, but it does not measure deaths per mile or risk across all miles driven.
